$comment: live: the current state (the open session, pit status, telemetry age, each service's health), so a client that joins late reads the current value at once and then watches it (ADR 0001, point 1). Every key carries its source (live, replay-<run>, parity). The keys are contracts' (subjects.yaml, paddock#72): ecu.status, ecu.session, ecu.pit and ecu.fuel of each source, written only by ecu (paddock#36, R3; paddock#73).
This file is not a stream config: bootstrap.sh turns each field into the flag of the same name for nats kv add and nats kv edit.
history 1: only the current value matters; a client that wants changes watches the key.
max_value_size 64 KiB (65536): a value is one status message as protobuf JSON, a few hundred bytes. 64 KiB is over 100 times that and still refuses a mistaken write of something frame-sized.

max_bucket_size 64 MiB (67108864): a handful of keys per source, each under 1 KB, so even thousands of replay runs leaving their keys behind fill a few MB. The limit is a backstop so the bucket cannot fill the disk.
No ttl: a value stays until it is replaced. Whether keys left by replays expire (per-key TTLs) is for the milestone that writes them.
Discard and duplicate window are not set here: nats kv add fixes them for every bucket (discard new, so a full bucket refuses a write rather than dropping a current value; a 2 min duplicate window).
replicas 1: one NATS server (ADR 0004). File storage so a server restart keeps the state.
description: Current state, one key per thing per source (paddock#36).
